content.title: About
content.content: Carrot is a root vegetable belonging to the Apiaceae family. It is cultivated worldwide and is one of the most popular vegetables. It has a mildly sweet, slightly earthy flavor and a crunchy texture when raw, becoming soft and sweet when cooked.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Carrots were domesticated in Central Asia over 5,000 years ago.
Originally carrots were purple, yellow or white; the orange variety became common in Europe in the 17th century.
The high beta‑carotene content gives orange carrots their color and converts to vitamin A in the body.
Carrots can be grown in soil or hydroponically, and their greens are sometimes used as herbs.
There are more than 100 carrot varieties differing in shape, color, and taste.

items.title: Rich in beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene is a precursor of vitamin A, essential for vision, immunity, and skin health.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Fiber, potassium, and antioxidants in carrots help lower blood pressure and cholesterol levels.

items.title: Boosts immune system
items.content: Vitamins C and K, as well as folate, contribute to a strong immune response.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: Both soluble and insoluble fiber improve intestinal motility and promote regular bowel movements.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Phytochemicals such as carotenoids and polyphenols combat free radicals and reduce the risk of chronic diseases.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Although rare, some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to carrots.

items.title: Excess vitamin A
items.content: Consuming large amounts of carrot concentrates or supplements can lead to hypervitaminosis A.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Eating large quantities of raw carrot may cause gas and discomfort in people with sensitive digestive systems.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Carrots can be eaten raw as sticks, added to salads, juices, and smoothies, as well as cooked in soups, stews, roasted, steamed, or sautéed. Grated carrot is often used in baked goods such as carrot cake and muffins.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store carrots in the refrigerator in a plastic bag or container, where they stay fresh for 2‑3 weeks. For longer storage, place them in an airtight bag and keep in a cool cellar or freezer, where they can last several months. Discard carrots showing signs of rot, softness, or off‑odors.
